description: MVCC decomposed. Postgres version chains in heap pages, hidden xmin/xmax columns, transaction visibility rules, vacuum. Oracle's undo segments. SQL Server's tempdb version store. The shared insight: writers create new versions; readers see version visible at transaction start.

sub_mechanisms.name: xmin_xmax_postgres
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hidden columns in every Postgres row: xmin = creating transaction ID, xmax = deleting transaction ID. Visibility derived from these.
sub_mechanisms.why: Row's life span = [xmin, xmax). Transaction T sees row if xmin committed before T started AND (xmax = 0 or xmax aborted or xmax > T). The visibility check at every read.

sub_mechanisms.name: transaction_id_xid
sub_mechanisms.definition: Monotonically increasing 32-bit ID assigned per transaction. Used in visibility checks + WAL.
sub_mechanisms.why: Identifies transactions for ordering + visibility. Postgres XIDs wrap at 2^32; vacuum freezes old rows to prevent wraparound corruption. 64-bit XIDs in some systems.

sub_mechanisms.name: snapshot_at_transaction_start
sub_mechanisms.definition: When transaction starts (or first reads), record: oldest active XID + set of currently-running XIDs. This snapshot determines visibility.
sub_mechanisms.why: Transaction sees: rows whose xmin committed before snapshot AND not in active set. Concurrent transactions invisible. Foundation of snapshot isolation.

sub_mechanisms.name: heap_only_tuple_HOT
sub_mechanisms.definition: Postgres optimisation: if UPDATE doesn't change indexed columns, new version stays on same page + indexes not updated.
sub_mechanisms.why: Avoids index write amplification on updates. New tuple linked from old via t_ctid. Reads follow chain to current visible version. Critical optimisation for update-heavy tables.

sub_mechanisms.name: version_chain
sub_mechanisms.definition: Doubly-linked list of row versions (old version → new via t_ctid). Multi-version visibility traversal walks the chain.
sub_mechanisms.why: Each visible-as-current version reached via chain traversal. Reads pay chain-length cost. Long chains (from many updates without vacuum) hurt performance.

sub_mechanisms.name: vacuum_old_versions
sub_mechanisms.definition: Postgres background process. Reclaims space from dead row versions (rows nothing can see). Updates freespace map + visibility map.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without vacuum: dead tuples accumulate (table bloat). Autovacuum runs based on row change ratio. Long-running transactions block vacuum → bloat.

sub_mechanisms.name: vacuum_freeze
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sets xmin to 'frozen XID' for very old rows. Prevents wraparound corruption (when XID space cycles).
sub_mechanisms.why: Postgres XIDs are 32-bit; wraparound destroys visibility. Vacuum freeze marks ancient rows as always-visible. Without periodic freeze, system can't tolerate XID wraparound — auto-vacuum addresses this.

sub_mechanisms.name: long_transaction_problem
sub_mechanisms.definition: Long-running transaction holds oldest snapshot. Vacuum can't reclaim versions newer than that snapshot.
sub_mechanisms.why: Long transactions = blocked vacuum = bloat. Postgres exposes pg_stat_activity to find them. Best practice: keep transactions short; analytical queries on read replica.

sub_mechanisms.name: oracle_undo_segment
sub_mechanisms.definition: Oracle stores old versions in separate undo tablespace. Reads of old versions reconstruct from undo records.
sub_mechanisms.why: Alternative to Postgres's in-heap versions. Old versions retrieved via undo apply (reverse changes). Pro: heap stays clean. Con: undo retention limited; ORA-01555 'snapshot too old' if undo recycled.

sub_mechanisms.name: sql_server_tempdb_version_store
sub_mechanisms.definition: SQL Server's row versioning. Old versions stored in tempdb. Used by READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT + SNAPSHOT isolation.
sub_mechanisms.why: tempdb can grow large under heavy versioning. Workload-specific tuning. Different design from Postgres + Oracle but same purpose.

sub_mechanisms.name: serializable_snapshot_isolation
sub_mechanisms.definition: SSI: snapshot isolation + detect serialization anomalies. Abort one of two conflicting transactions instead of waiting.
sub_mechanisms.why: Postgres SERIALIZABLE level. Catches write skew that plain snapshot misses. Cost: false aborts under contention. The way to get serializable without pessimistic locking.

sub_mechanisms.name: commit_timestamp
sub_mechanisms.definition: Some systems record actual commit time per transaction (vs XID's monotonic counter). Used by Spanner for external consistency.
sub_mechanisms.why: External consistency: if T1 commits before T2 in real time, T1's effects visible to T2. Spanner uses TrueTime to provide this. Stronger than serializability.

derivation_rules.name: MVCC_readers_see_consistent_snapshot
if: a transaction snapshots active XIDs at start
then: reads see only data committed before that point
derivation_rules.why: Visibility check: xmin committed AND not in active set AND (xmax = 0 or aborted or > snapshot). Mathematical isolation. Foundation of snapshot isolation in Postgres + Oracle + SQL Server.

derivation_rules.name: HOT_avoids_index_write_amplification
derivation_rules.why: Old + new tuple on same page; old tuple's t_ctid points to new. Indexes still point to old, but reads chase the chain to new. Postgres update-heavy tables depend on this optimisation.

derivation_rules.name: long_transactions_block_vacuum
if: a transaction holds the oldest snapshot
then: vacuum cannot reclaim versions newer than that snapshot
derivation_rules.why: Vacuum could reclaim a version the long transaction would later read. Conservative: keep all versions newer than oldest snapshot. Production rule: monitor + kill old transactions to prevent bloat.

derivation_rules.name: SSI_detects_write_skew
if: transactions form a dangerous cycle in dependency graph
then: SSI aborts one to preserve serializability
derivation_rules.why: Snapshot isolation misses write skew. SSI tracks read + write sets, detects cycles. Aborts cheaper than locking. Cost: false aborts under contention; retry logic required in app code.

derivation_rules.name: vacuum_freeze_prevents_XID_wraparound
then: periodic freeze of ancient rows is required
derivation_rules.why: 2^32 XIDs ~ 4 billion. Without freeze, ancient row's xmin appears 'in future' after wraparound. Postgres aggressively warns + then refuses connections at wraparound risk. Auto-vacuum freeze is mandatory operational concern.
